t5.condition: prong A (pre-registered): median over 5 blocks of (slower baseline achieved / flashdb achieved) <= 1.5; prong B (ticket-80 cross-check): flashdb sustained the rung under the unified rule in at least 4 of 5 blocks
t5.defect: the baselines did not sustain the 1x rung in enough blocks ({'sqlite': 0, 'postgres': 2}), so the sustained-level comparison has no baseline denominator; this weakens T6, not T5, and it is disclosed rather than smoothed
t5.threshold: T5 low-load non-inferiority: at the 1x rung flashdb must be within 1.5x of the slower baseline (2x is the fail line, 10x a design failure)

t6.condition: a level R is common when every arm sustained it in at least 4 of 5 blocks; T6 reads flashdb's median achieved at the highest such R against the best baseline's median achieved at the same R
t6.defect: no offered level was sustained by every arm in enough blocks, or flashdb's sustained level there is below 3x the best baseline
t6.fix: extend the ladder above the highest common level and re-run the rungs where an arm was rejected, so a common sustained level above it can exist
t6.threshold: T6 high-load superiority: at the highest common offered level flashdb must reach at least 3x the best baseline's sustained throughput under the same latency rule

t7.condition: the declared arm's own T5 prongs at the 1x rung
t7.defect: the baselines did not sustain the 1x rung in enough blocks ({'sqlite': 0, 'postgres': 2}), so the sustained-level comparison has no baseline denominator; this weakens T6, not T5, and it is disclosed rather than smoothed
t7.disclosure: flashdb-learned was not run: M1 wires no learner controller, so a second flashdb arm would measure the same declared wiring twice
t7.threshold: T7 initial-policy quality: the declared arm alone must pass T5
